historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case average organic growth FY2027-FY2031 (12, 9, 7.5, 7, 6.5). Equity 5yr CAGR (13.2%) and revenue 5yr CAGR (14.4%) include debt-funded M&A and the FY2025-26 photonics spike and are not a forward organic proxy; management's long-run organic target is ~7%.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC charge - total lease cash (FY2021: 235.4-13.4-16.4=205.6; FY2023: 212.1-19.6-21.0=171.5; FY2026: 409.6-30.1-29.3=350.2). The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR (26.9%) is flattered by a working-capital-heavy FY2023 trough (cash conversion ~70%); the 5yr figure (11.2%) is the representative one and sits slightly BELOW the reported 5yr FCF CAGR (11.7%) because SBC (13.4m -> 30.1m, 2.2x) and lease cash have grown faster than cash flow. Equity CAGR is within 30% of both revenue and EPS CAGRs: no divergence flag.

scenario_narratives.base: Halma delivers FY2027 as guided at the September 2026 trading update: low-double-digit organic growth with ~5pp from photonics (growing ~30%, down from 52%) and an adjusted EBIT margin of 23.5-24%. The photonics premium then fades over two years as the optical-switch programme matures and the hyperscaler customer's share of Group revenue plateaus around 20% and dilutes, leaving the other ~45 companies compounding at Halma's long-run ~7% organic trend before easing to 4% by FY2036. Margins hold at the FY2027 level; cash conversion stays ~90% with working capital absorbing ~17% of each year's revenue increase. M&A continues at GBP 400-500m/yr but is NPV-neutral in the model, so the value here is the organic cash stream only.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI data-centre build-out runs for several more years and Avo Photonics wins the next two generations of co-designed optical switch, with a second hyperscaler diversifying the concentration; the order book ahead of revenue (Sept 2026) converts into 14% growth in FY2027 and 10-12% through FY2029. Operating leverage and pricing lift adjusted EBIT margin toward 25%, the top of Halma's historical range, and the group re-earns its compounder premium. Terminal growth 3%, same 8.5% WACC.
scenario_narratives.bear: The June 2026 de-rating was the first signal, not the last: the single hyperscaler customer (~20% of FY2026 revenue, up from 12% two years ago) pauses or re-sources optical-switch capacity in FY2028, taking photonics down ~30% and Group organic growth to zero for a year while the above-Group-margin business de-leverages (adjusted EBIT margin ~21%). The remaining portfolio is sound but grows at the bottom of its historical 4-5% organic range, the record GBP 900m+ of FY2026-27 acquisitions carry integration risk under new sector leadership (E&A sector CE left for Spectris, CTO departing), and the market stops paying for an AI premium (terminal cap 18x). No solvency issue: net debt/EBITDA 1.16x against a 3.5x covenant, so this is a growth-and-multiple bear, not a balance-sheet one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the organic owner-FCF stream of a decentralised, high-return niche industrial at a GBP-built 8.5% WACC, charging SBC and IFRS-16 lease cash in the flows once each and treating Halma's large and continuous M&A programme as NPV-neutral. The deliberate consequence is that this model does not credit the thing the market has historically paid ~30x earnings for: 20+ years of redeploying cash into bolt-ons at returns above WACC. The gap between the model's weighted value and the price is therefore an explicit statement of how much of today's price rests on (a) the AI photonics premium persisting and (b) continued value-accretive M&A, rather than a claim that the market is simply wrong. The required-return table says what return the current price implies on the base organic path.
key_risks_to_valuation: Single hyperscaler customer at ~20% of Group revenue (12% in FY2024) in an AI-capex-cyclical photonics niche; a pause is the bear case and carries 30% weight
Base case assumes the photonics premium fades gently rather than reversing; a sharper reversal pushes base toward bear

M&A treated as NPV-neutral: if Halma keeps compounding acquired capital at ~14-15% ROTIC, intrinsic value is understated; if the record GBP 900m+ of FY2026-27 deals integrates poorly, it is overstated via the base growth path
Terminal value is the majority of EV at 8.5% WACC / 2.5% g; each 50bp of WACC moves the base value by roughly 8-10%
52% USD revenue: sterling strength is a persistent translation drag (FY2026 -2.7% revenue); flows are modelled in GBP at the September 2026 FX assumption
Cash tax modelled at 24% on unlevered EBIT vs ~20% actually paid in FY2026: conservative by ~GBP 25-30m/yr if the timing benefit persists
Leadership transition: Environmental & Analysis sector CE departed to competitor Spectris, CTO leaving, in a model that depends on a deep bench of entrepreneurial managers

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (LSE regular close); 52-week range 3268-4902 GBp
data_sources.financials: HLMA.L_Metrics.csv (FY2019-FY2026 annual + half-years, extraction gate clean); FY2026 Annual Report: consolidated cash flow statement (Extracted/HLMA.L_Annual_FY2026.txt:11374-11423), EPS note diluted shares (:12491-12495), leases note 28 (:14394-14455: ROU depreciation 26.4, lease interest 4.3, total lease cash 29.3), balance sheet working capital (:11254-11276)
data_sources.qualitative: HLMA.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): FY2026 results June 2026, 24 Sept 2026 trading update guidance (low-double-digit organic, 23.5-24% adjusted EBIT margin, ~30% photonics growth, capex GBP 55-60m, ETR 23.5-24%, central costs ~GBP 60m, FX -GBP 8m revenue), hyperscaler customer concentration disclosure

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average diluted shares FY2026 (377.7m basic + 1.5m dilutive share awards = 379.2m, FY2026 AR EPS note). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows and the employee benefit trust buys shares in the market to settle awards (GBP 33.5m in FY2026), so the count has been flat at ~378-379m since FY2019.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF = reported FCF 409.6 (OCF 480.6 less capex 71.0: PPE 54.9 + software 1.0 + other intangibles 0.3 + capitalised development 14.8) minus SBC charge 30.1 minus total lease cash 29.3 (25.0 principal + 4.3 interest, FY2026 AR note 28) minus interest income 0 = 350.2. Interest income (GBP 6.0m) is NOT stripped because the company is a net borrower (net debt 2.0x owner FCF); interest received sits in investing and interest paid in financing, so OCF is already pre-interest and there is no interest double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR income statement note: share-based payment charge GBP 30.1m (FY2025 26.3m). The cash-flow add-back is lower (17.2m) because part of the charge is cash-settled/EBT-funded; the P&L charge is the economic cost and is used. No separate equity-award tax line is disclosed (nil).
inputs.buyback_note: GBP 33.5m is 'purchase of shares for settlement of employee share arrangements' (EBT market purchases), not a repurchase programme. It is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and is already charged via the SBC deduction; Halma has run no buyback programme in the period.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP/share to quoted pence. Single listing, no parity check available; magnitude check: FY2026 adjusted EPS 114.05p vs price 3528p = 30.9x.
inputs.price_note: LSE regular close (16:35 BST). Not an after-hours print.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP: UK 10y gilt ~4.5% risk-free, 5.0% equity risk premium, beta ~0.85 (low-cyclicality safety/health/environmental niches) gives cost of equity ~8.75%; pre-tax cost of debt 3.8% (weighted average rate on gross debt 3.77% per FY2026 AR), ~2.9% post-tax; market-value weights ~94% equity / 6% debt (GBP 13.4bn market cap vs GBP 0.8bn gross debt) give ~8.4%. Rounded to 8.5% and held identical across all three scenarios: customer-concentration and AI-capex-cycle risk are charged in the bear flows and the bear weight, not in the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: total lease cash of GBP 29.3m (25.0m principal in financing + 4.3m interest, FY2026 AR note 28, 'total cash outflows for leases') is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (1.1% of revenue), and lease liabilities (GBP 107.8m = 82.6 non-current + 25.2 current) are EXCLUDED from net debt. Net debt used is therefore 662.2 (borrowings 805.6 less cash 143.4), not the company's lease-inclusive 769.1. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (67.0 - 26.4 ROU = 40.6, 1.57% of revenue) so the lease is charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: None required: FY2026 profit attributable to owners (372.3) equals Group profit; no material non-controlling interests.
inputs.acquisition_treatment: Halma's model is ~2/3 organic / ~1/3 M&A (GBP 447m across five deals in FY2026, a further GBP 515m across six deals disclosed by the 24 Sept 2026 trading update). Projections are ORGANIC growth only from the FY2026 base; acquisitions are treated as NPV-neutral (cash out = value in), so neither post-balance-date deal spend nor acquired revenue is in the model. FY2027 base growth includes ~1pp of annualisation of FY2026 deals, whose cash is already in the 31 March 2026 net debt. This is the deliberate house conservatism: the market's premium multiple partly pays for Halma's record of deploying M&A capital at ROTIC (~14-15%) well above WACC, which this model does not credit.
inputs.ebitda_basis: ebitda_margin_path is adjusted EBITDA BEFORE SBC and before lease cost (post-IFRS-16 reported adjusted EBITDA 661.5 + SBC 30.1 = 691.6, 26.8% of FY2026 revenue), so that the engine's SBC and lease deductions land back on the reported basis. Component tie-out FY2026: 691.6 - 30.1 SBC - 29.3 lease - 40.6 D&A ex-ROU = 591.6 vs adjusted EBIT 594.5 less lease interest 4.3 = 590.2.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon, probability-weighted three scenarios, routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md (operating company, non-US industrial: adaptations applied for GBP-built WACC, GBp quote, IFRS-16 leases). Fresh build, no prior DCF. Halma is a decentralised group of ~45 niche safety/environmental/healthcare technology companies; value is a cash-flow stream, so the owner-FCF route is correct. Key structural judgment: FY2026 organic growth of 16.6% included ~8pp from AI data-centre photonics (Avo Photonics optical switches) where a single hyperscaler customer is now ~20% of Group revenue (12% FY2024, 15% FY2025). The base case takes management's FY2027 'low double-digit' organic guidance (incl. ~5pp photonics at ~30% growth) and then fades toward Halma's long-run ~7% organic trend and below; it does NOT extrapolate the FY2026 spike. Bear weight is raised to 30% for the single-customer dependency. Cash tax is modelled on unlevered EBIT at the guided 23.5-24% ETR (cash taxes paid were 112.5m, ~20% of adjusted PBT, i.e. timing-flattered); the interest tax shield lives in the after-tax cost of debt. Working capital: inventories 322.2 + receivables 601.0 - payables 421.5 = 501.7 (19.4% of revenue) so growth consumes cash; wc_capture -17% of incremental revenue (FY2026 cash conversion 93%).

bear.growth_rationale: FY2027 lands at 8% (H1 already strong, order book covers much of the year) but the hyperscaler customer pauses optical-switch capex in FY2028: photonics (~20% of revenue) falls ~30%, a ~6pp drag that offsets ~6% growth in the other ~45 companies, so Group organic growth is flat. Recovery to 3% then a 4-5% trend: Halma ex-photonics at the low end of its historical organic range with the AI premium gone for good.
bear.margin_rationale: Photonics is above-Group-margin and has capacity in place; a volume pause de-leverages it. Adjusted EBIT margin falls to ~21% (EBITDA pre-SBC 25%) and recovers only to 21.5% as central costs and R&D (4.7% of revenue) are held. Terminal cap 18x reflects a business the market no longer prices as an AI beneficiary.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 12% = management's low-double-digit organic guidance (~11%, of which ~5pp photonics at ~30%) plus ~1pp annualisation of FY2026 acquisitions, less ~0.3pp sterling headwind (-GBP 8m). Photonics premium then fades (9% FY2028, 7.5% FY2029) toward the ~7% long-run organic trend, and below it from FY2031 as the base matures; terminal 2.5%.
base.margin_rationale: FY2027 EBITDA (pre-SBC, pre-lease) 27.5% = guided 23.5-24% adjusted EBIT margin midpoint + 1.1% lease + 1.6% D&A ex-ROU + 1.15% SBC, vs 26.8% FY2026. Only +20bps further to 27.7% as photonics mix fades and central costs rise (~GBP 60m guided).
base.capex_rationale: FY2027 PPE guided GBP 55-60m plus ~GBP 15m capitalised development and ~1m software = ~2.6% of revenue (2.75% FY2026), easing to 2.3% as capacity programmes complete. Capex stays above D&A ex-ROU (1.6%) throughout: a growing manufacturer.

bull.growth_rationale: Order intake ahead of revenue and prior year (Sept 2026 update) carries FY2027 to the top of low-double-digit plus annualisation (14%); photonics sustains ~30% for two more generations of optical switch with a second hyperscaler customer, keeping Group organic growth at 10-12% through FY2029 before fading to trend. Still organic only; M&A NPV-neutral.
bull.margin_rationale: Operating leverage on photonics volume and 1-2% pricing lift adjusted EBIT margin toward 25% (EBITDA pre-SBC 29%), the upper end of Halma's historical range.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30% because of a single-customer dependency the method explicitly names as grounds to do so: one hyperscaler is ~20% of revenue in a capex-cyclical end market, and management itself says the photonics growth profile 'differs from the wider Group in pace, scale and longevity'. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right (AI capex persists, Avo wins the next switch generations, a second customer diversifies the book). Base 50%: the September 2026 guidance has order intake ahead of revenue behind it and H1 FY2027 is largely in hand.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
trip_reasons: sanity_check.py historical_table()/implied_multiples() fx_rate direction bug on this GBP/GBp ticker (see sanity_check_note) -- forced to false so an automated pass built on nonsense arithmetic does not silently clear the eval gate
diagnosis: see sanity_check_note for hand-bridged multiples; no DCF driver changes needed

sanity_check_note.bug_reference: sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-systemic-bug (memory) -- scripts/sanity_check.py historical_table() multiplies the GBp price series by fx_rate=100 instead of dividing, and does the same to current_price before computing implied_multiples. HLMA.L is GBP-reporting/GBp-quote like BAB.L/EZJ.L/FRAS.L/DCC.L, all previously confirmed hit by this bug.
sanity_check_note.symptom: script printed historical pb_avg 61902x, ev_ebitda_avg 226295x, p_sales_avg 53220x, and implied pb 441.8x, ev_ebitda 1518.0x, p_sales 370.9x -- all ~100x too high because FY-end prices were multiplied by 100 instead of divided (pence treated as needing conversion to pounds via multiplication, not division).
sanity_check_note.method: hand-bridged by dividing each FY-end price (from HLMA.L_Prices.csv) by 100 to get GBP pounds, then market_cap = price_gbp * shares_outstanding, compared against ShareholdersEquity / EBITDA / Revenue from HLMA.L_Metrics.csv, net_debt = TotalDebt - Cash.
sanity_check_note.verdict: Genuine pass. Base-case IV implies P/B 4.42x, EV/EBITDA 15.5x and P/Sales 3.71x, all at or below the 10-year historical range (P/B 4.80-8.41x, EV/EBITDA 18.4-29.5x, P/Sales 4.09-7.45x) -- consistent with the conservative organic-only (no M&A NPV) approach the dcf-analyst used. The current price (P/B 6.15x, EV/EBITDA 21.2x, P/Sales 5.16x) sits comfortably inside the historical range too, so the -28% upside reflects growth/M&A premium in the price, not a DCF that is priced outside Halma's own trading history.
